Q: In an HTML table, what's the use of the scope attribute for <tr>, <tg>, and <td> A:

A cell is related to a header if it's within the category designated by that header. If scope = "row", the header refers to all data within its own row. If scope = "col", the header refers to all data within its own column.

For an example, take a look at the DEMO section in the article you reference. You can see that the column header "Player" refers to players TR-7, Khiresh Odo, and Mia Oolong, while the header "Gloobles" corresponds to 7, 7, and 9, which I guess are the numbers of Gloobles for each player. (No idea what a Glooble is, but let's think of it as like a score.) Meanwhile, the row header "TR-7" shows that the values in that row all correspond to the Player TR-7. So TR-7 has 7 Gloobles. That's why "Player" has scope = "col" and "TR-7" has scope = "row".

Extremely important note: scope doesn't change ANYTHING about the actual table layout! It just makes changes to help people understand the table layout. Scope does two things:

  • Colors in headers based on row or column, so it's easier for people to visually understand how the table works. I would suggest that you change the scope of different <th> cells from "row" to "col" to see this in the DEMO section I discussed above. Notice how it's possible to create a very confusing table as well as an easy-to-understand table.

  • Explicitly adds the info that cells are headers so that people who use screen readers can better understand what's going on. (You can imagine how things would get confusing when there are row headers AND column headers). This is explained in depth in the article I linked below.

For more info about how this helps people who use screen readers, as well as other disabled people, here is the full article about making HTML tables accessible. It explains how scope can be used for "row" and "col", but also for "rowgroup" and "colgroup". If you need rowgroup and colgroup, you'll need to read this article and play with the demos shown. Basically, this lets a header refer to multiple rows or columns, because those rows or columns are in the same category. You may also want to look through the <th> section of table basics.

Q: Django - concatenating multiple HttpResponses for partial templates A:

Can this be done on the database side by concatenating HttpResponse objects

I think you mean server side? Responses aren't generated by the database.

Regardless though, no you can't concatenate responses, a request can only have one response. You can either create different views where each one returns the data you're looking for and then make multiple requests on the frontend. Or, you can return JSON where each key is the data you need.

Q: How to run jq from gitbash in windows? A:

You may deal with that in PowerShell even when there's no jq because it has built-in support for various structured text formats like JSON, XML, CSV... The file can be parsed directly into .NET objects that you can manipulate easily. For this purpose you can use ConvertFrom-Json and ConvertTo-Json

# Open the json file and modify the properties
$config = Get-Content -Path "config.json" | ConvertFrom-Json
$config.AppSettings.LogLevel = "Info"
$config.ServiceSettings.MaxUsers = 200

# Convert the modified object back and save it:
$config | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3 | Set-Content -Path "config.json"

See also

  • PowerShell : retrieve JSON object by field value
  • Playing with JSON and PowerShell
  • Working with JSON data in PowerShell
  • PowerShell and JSON: A Practical Guide
  • Parsing JSON with PowerShell

Q: Threading flask and while loop A:

Python argument list is always evaluated first and the result is then passed to the function being called. In your case app.run() is executed/evaluated first, and then it's passed to threading.Thread() as its argument. That's why you notice it's executed first because Python needs to get the result from app.run() first. So if that argument is changed to app.run then it is a method object instead of calling for its result. You can then pass such object to threading.Thread()'s keyword parameter target= so in that function in can be executed in its separate thread.

The same goes to loop(), which should be changed to loop so the code can pass another method object to threading.Thread() to execute in another separate thread. Without doing so, you are simply executing the loop in the main thread.

So these 2 lines:

thread1 = threading.Thread(target=app.run())
thread2 = threading.Thread(target=loop())

should be changed to:

thread1 = threading.Thread(target=app.run)
thread2 = threading.Thread(target=loop)

Q: Java client using SAAJ error: SEVERE: SAAJ0008: Bad Response; Unauthorized A:

I realize this is an old question but would like to leave some assistance to anyone in the future who ends up here (like I did). There is a few likely situations that I have recently experienced regarding this.

  1. Check that your details are correct, or that the connection is possible. Be 100% sure before moving on.
  2. You will receive an unauthorized error if your database is not correctly configured for some setups (for instance, on JBoss). In my situation the data-source file was not being read properly when it attempted to connect causing the Unauthorized error on the client side.

Q: How to avoid getting java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: org/apache/commons/logging/LogFactory A:

Commons Logging needs to be added to the classpath. If you're working in a regular Netbeans project (and not in a Maven project in Netbeans) check out this SO question or this article that explain how to add libraries to a project.

If on the other hand you're working on a Maven project using Netbeans, Commons logging has to be added as a dependency. How that's done can be found here - basically it's a rightclick on the libraries node in the project tree, add dependency, enter artefact details or use the built-in search assistant to locate the correct artefact in the Maven repository.
